section_summary: This section records Japanese notifications under the 1930 London Naval Treaty about destroyers and a minelayer, alongside American acknowledgments and Navy Department copies. It then follows reports and diplomatic exchanges about Japanese battleship construction, especially whether the training ship Hiyei was being remilitarized. Later documents concern naval fuel purchases, vessels reportedly built in France, a Japanese Navy purchasing office in New York, steelmaking equipment, and Japan’s 1939 naval estimates.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of destroyer notification
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japanese particulars for a destroyer whose keel had been laid.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Ambassador Saito’s October 9 notice under Article 10 of the London Naval Treaty.

subfiles.title: Completion of Shiratsuyu and Shigure
subfiles.about: Reports completion and specifications of two Japanese destroyers.
subfiles.summary: Provides completion dates, displacement, dimensions and gun calibers for Shiratsuyu and Shigure under Article 10.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Shiratsuyu and Shigure completion
subfiles.about: Acknowledges completion particulars for Shiratsuyu and Shigure.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the embassy’s October 27 treaty notification.

subfiles.title: Destroyer particulars forwarded to the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese note on completed destroyers.
subfiles.summary: Sends the Navy Department a copy of the Japanese destroyer notification.

subfiles.title: Completion of Okino Shima
subfiles.about: Reports completion and specifications of the Japanese minelayer Okino Shima.
subfiles.summary: Lists the minelayer’s completion date, displacement, dimensions and largest gun.

subfiles.title: Okino Shima particulars forwarded to the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese completion notice for Okino Shima.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the ambassador’s November 16 note for Navy files.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Okino Shima completion
subfiles.about: Acknowledges particulars of the completed minelayer Okino Shima.
subfiles.summary: Thanks the ambassador for the treaty notification.

subfiles.title: Keel laying of Yamakumo
subfiles.about: Reports the keel laying and specifications of destroyer Yamakumo.
subfiles.summary: States that Yamakumo’s keel was laid November 4, 1936.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Yamakumo notification
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japan’s Yamakumo keel-laying notice.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the February 8 note and its treaty particulars.

subfiles.title: Yamakumo particulars forwarded to the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards Yamakumo’s keel-laying particulars.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Japanese Embassy’s February 8 note.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on naval rearmament
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on American, British and Japanese naval rearmament.
subfiles.summary: References a March 12 meeting and an attached British rearmament memorandum.

subfiles.title: Keel laying of Kasumi and Asagumo
subfiles.about: Reports keel laying and specifications of two Japanese destroyers.
subfiles.summary: Gives dates and technical particulars for Kasumi and Asagumo under Article 10.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Kasumi and Asagumo notification
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the two destroyer keel-laying notices.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the embassy’s March 30 note.

subfiles.title: Kasumi and Asagumo particulars forwarded to the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese notice concerning Kasumi and Asagumo.
subfiles.summary: Provides the Navy Department with the destroyer particulars.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on Japanese capital ships
subfiles.about: Reports an impending interview denying rumors of oversized Japanese battleships.
subfiles.summary: The embassy notes continuing uncertainty and restricted attaché visits to Kure and Yokosuka.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Tokyo telegram 133
subfiles.about: Restates the embassy’s report on battleship rumors and the Yonai interview.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrases the original telegram on ship size, guns and naval-yard access.

subfiles.title: Japan denies naval threat
subfiles.about: Presents Admiral Yonai’s answers about Japanese naval policy and big-gun rumors.
subfiles.summary: Yonai denies plans for threatening armament or guns larger than 16 inches.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on battleship size
subfiles.about: References a report doubting Japan will build ships above 35,000 tons.
subfiles.summary: Points to a separately filed memorandum on Japanese battleships.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on new Japanese battleships
subfiles.about: References a report of Japanese battleships carrying ten 16-inch guns.
subfiles.summary: Points to a separately filed despatch.

subfiles.title: Riga despatch enclosing Stirling article
subfiles.about: Encloses a Riga newspaper article by Rear Admiral Yates Stirling.
subfiles.summary: Lane forwards “Offensive in the Pacific” and says no full translation is included.

subfiles.title: Offensive in the Pacific
subfiles.about: Discusses Pacific naval strategy and the possibility of very large Japanese battleships.
subfiles.summary: The German-language article argues that American Pacific commitments require offensive naval capacity. It discusses bases, the Panama Canal and reported Japanese plans for fast battleships with 45-centimeter guns. It warns that such ships could trigger construction of similar vessels by other powers.

subfiles.title: Summary translation of Offensive in the Pacific
subfiles.about: Summarizes Stirling’s article on Pacific defense and 50,000-ton battleships.
subfiles.summary: The translation describes American obligations in the Pacific, compares naval bases and warns that reported Japanese 50,000-ton ships would spur matching construction. It also discusses treaty limits and the Panama Canal.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese Navy oil purchases
subfiles.about: References a Netherlands inquiry about Japanese Navy oil purchases in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Points to a separately filed memorandum and Netherlands Legation attachment.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on battleship preparations
subfiles.about: References a memorandum on Japanese preparations for battleship construction.
subfiles.summary: Points to a separately filed memorandum.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on limits and naval race
subfiles.about: References doubts that Japan would provoke a race with oversized battleships.
subfiles.summary: Points to a telegram concerning 35,000-ton ships and guns exceeding 14 inches.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on oil information exchange
subfiles.about: References a proposed exchange of Japanese Navy oil-purchase figures.
subfiles.summary: Records Dutch agreement to exchange East Indies and American purchase information.

subfiles.title: British aide-mémoire on Hiyei
subfiles.about: Seeks American support against possible remilitarization of the Japanese battleship Hiyei.
subfiles.summary: Britain argues that the 1930 treaty’s training-ship disposal provisions remain binding after expiry. It says Hiyei’s return to combat service would upset relative naval strength and asks whether the United States will make parallel representations to Japan.

subfiles.title: European Affairs memorandum on Hiyei
subfiles.about: Highlights the British request for parallel American representations on Hiyei.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the legal dispute and the British plan to seek Japan’s intentions.

subfiles.title: Request for Navy views on Hiyei
subfiles.about: Requests Navy Department views on possible Hiyei remilitarization.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the British aide-mémoire.

subfiles.title: Navy Department opinion on Hiyei
subfiles.about: Supports the British treaty interpretation concerning Hiyei.
subfiles.summary: The Navy recommends opposing remilitarization of ships retained exclusively for training.

subfiles.title: American reply to British aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: States American agreement that Hiyei cannot lawfully be remilitarized.
subfiles.summary: The United States accepts Britain’s interpretation of the 1930 treaty and says its ambassador in Tokyo will raise the matter if Japanese intentions warrant it.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Grew on Hiyei
subfiles.about: Directs informal inquiry and possible representations concerning Hiyei.
subfiles.summary: Grew is to establish Japanese intentions and, if remilitarization is planned, state that training ships disposed of under the treaty cannot return to active service. He is to seek further instructions if formal protest appears necessary.

subfiles.title: Hiyei correspondence forwarded to the Navy
subfiles.about: Sends the Navy copies of the British reply and Tokyo instruction.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Navy views and encloses subsequent State Department correspondence.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on oversized Japanese capital ships
subfiles.about: References reports that Japan may be building ships above the 35,000-ton limit.
subfiles.summary: Points to a separately filed British telegram.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on Hiyei and capital ships
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese denial that Hiyei is being remilitarized and conflicting battleship rumors.
subfiles.summary: A senior aide says Hiyei is being repaired solely as a training ship, which the Naval Attaché finds credible. Other attachés still believe new Japanese capital ships will exceed 40,000 tons.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram forwarded to the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards a confidential paraphrase of Grew’s Hiyei telegram.
subfiles.summary: Sends the January 26 Tokyo report for Navy records.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting delay on Hiyei decision
subfiles.about: Asks that a final decision on Hiyei await the Naval Attaché’s written report.
subfiles.summary: Identifies report 20-38 as en route by diplomatic pouch.

subfiles.title: European Affairs note on Italian battleship report
subfiles.about: Explains how a report of 46,000-ton Japanese battleships was obtained from naval intelligence.
subfiles.summary: The division found no earlier State Department copy of the Rome attaché report.

subfiles.title: Handwritten search note on battleship report
subfiles.about: Notes the absence of an embassy or military attaché report on 46,000-ton battleships.
subfiles.summary: Records an unsuccessful file search.

subfiles.title: ONI report translating Japan and Her Fleet
subfiles.about: Translates an Italian press article claiming major Japanese fleet expansion.
subfiles.summary: The article claims Japan is building three 46,000-ton battleships and projects a much larger fleet by 1941. It links Japanese naval expansion to treaty expiry, Pacific bases and strategic competition.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Edwin C. Hill broadcast
subfiles.about: References a complaint about Edwin C. Hill’s broadcast on Japanese naval building.
subfiles.summary: Points to a letter, telegram and broadcast excerpt filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Grew despatch on Hiyei
subfiles.about: Transmits the Naval Attaché’s report on possible Hiyei remilitarization.
subfiles.summary: Encloses report 20-38, cited in the embassy’s February 1 telegram.

subfiles.title: Naval Attaché report 20-38 on Hiyei
subfiles.about: Evaluates a Japanese denial of Hiyei’s remilitarization.
subfiles.summary: A senior aide says Hiyei’s work supports its continued use as a training ship and denies additions to armor, boilers or turrets. The attaché reviews contrary clues: prolonged dockyard work, restricted access, budget figures and foreign reports. He considers the aide credible but notes that the conversation was unofficial.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese naval construction
subfiles.about: References a separate Naval Attaché report on Japanese construction.
subfiles.summary: Points to confidential report 45, dated February 18.

subfiles.title: British aide-mémoire withdrawing Hiyei representations
subfiles.about: Says Britain no longer proposes to pursue representations about Hiyei.
subfiles.summary: Britain now believes Hiyei has been remilitarized and sees little prospect of a satisfactory response.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Grew despatch on Hiyei
subfiles.about: Repeats the February 1 despatch transmitting report 20-38.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of the despatch on Hiyei.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Naval Attaché report 20-38
subfiles.about: Repeats the attaché’s evaluation of Hiyei’s dockyard work.
subfiles.summary: This is a second, noisier copy of the report on the aide’s denial and evidence suggesting extensive work on Hiyei. It retains the attaché’s cautious judgment that the denial seemed truthful but was unofficial.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of British Hiyei aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Britain’s decision to drop further Hiyei representations.
subfiles.summary: Notes the British assessment without substantive comment.

subfiles.title: British Hiyei position forwarded to the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the July British aide-mémoire and State Department reply.
subfiles.summary: Updates the Navy on Britain’s changed Hiyei position.

subfiles.title: British Hiyei position forwarded to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sends the British July aide-mémoire to Grew.
subfiles.summary: States that the Department acknowledged the British communication without comment.

subfiles.title: Japanese Navy gasoline order
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum on a Japanese Navy order for high-grade gasoline.
subfiles.summary: Suggests the information may interest the Naval Attaché.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on gasoline purchase
subfiles.about: Details a reported Japanese Navy purchase of gasoline from Gulf Oil.
subfiles.summary: Gives specifications, price, payment arrangements and shipment schedule for 50,000 drums.

subfiles.title: Reported launches under construction in France
subfiles.about: Transmits an unconfirmed report of armed launches being built for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Paris embassy sends Higgins’s memorandum and says French officials will investigate.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tamaris-sur-Mer launches
subfiles.about: Describes reported construction of small armed boats for Japan near Toulon.
subfiles.summary: An English informant reports seeing about a dozen shallow-draft boats at Tamaris-sur-Mer, apparently intended for river use.

subfiles.title: Navy inquiry about Japanese purchasing office
subfiles.about: Requests information on a Japanese Navy purchasing office established in New York.
subfiles.summary: The Navy says its only record is a 1917 embassy notification.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on foreign agents
subfiles.about: Recommends better records on foreign government personnel and offices in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Prompted by the lack of information on the Japanese Navy’s New York office, the division proposes collecting duties, dates and biographical details for foreign government representatives. It recommends a circular to diplomatic missions and a readily searchable departmental record.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese purchasing office
subfiles.about: Answers the Navy’s request for information about the Japanese purchasing office.
subfiles.summary: State reports that a file search found nothing beyond the 1917 notice.

subfiles.title: Visas for Daido Steel engineers
subfiles.about: Reports visas issued to three Japanese engineers visiting American steel facilities.
subfiles.summary: The Daido Steel engineers plan to inspect Ajax machinery in Ohio before its shipment to Japan. The consul notes Daido’s extensive Japanese Navy work and gives their travel and American contact details.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on fourth naval estimates
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s proposed Fourth Naval Replenishment Program.
subfiles.summary: Grew gives a total of roughly 1.67 billion yen for ships, facilities and naval aviation. He compares the increases with the Third Program and notes that refitting and stores may remain under that earlier program.
